content.comment_body: Hi, I have a [product_name] with article number [article_no]. My installed version of [product_name] software is [version_no] and I'm running it in a virtual machine (VMware Player). I am unable to connect between my PC and the [product_name], making it impossible to transfer programs. Despite successful pings both ways, each connection attempt triggers an error (see screen_1.png). Even when creating a network project in [product_name] software, the device is detected online but connection still fails. Interestingly, with another version ([article_no]) and the same setup, communication works without issue. Any ideas how to resolve this?

To upload to a [product_name] with [article_no], it must be set to admin-mode. Please check in the hardware setup for administrator mode and enter password "[user_name]". After this you should be able to load the module.
Yes, the device is in admin mode, but I am still unable to connect.

Have you tried restarting the [product_name] software or the VMware Player or PC after receiving the warning? This message is known, but usually restarting the software or the PC resolves it. Also, verify if your Ethernet interface is configured correctly and the appropriate interface is selected from the drop-down in the software. In VMware, the LAN interface should also be configured independently. Ensure both device and interface IP addresses are on the same subnet. Hope this helps.

It seems the issue is related to the virtual environment. When the software detects the device and PC in different subnets, it adds an IP to the VM, which doesn't affect your host machine, leading to connection problems. Consider installing the software directly on your host instead of the VM. Since it's a Java application, it shouldn't significantly impact system performance like other programs.

I have a similar issue. [product_name] software [version_no] is installed on a physical PC running Windows XP Pro SP3. Two modules are in admin mode and I've tried restarting both the software and the PC after the warning, but the problem persists. Communication with an earlier software version works fine. I've uploaded a .zip video displaying IP, subnet mask, and LAN interface settings. Any advice would be appreciated.

From your video, it appears there's an issue with the Ethernet card as the name doesn't display correctly in the software. This could prevent the software from manipulating the interface, especially with new features in [version_no]. Try renaming the Ethernet card so it's properly recognized, or using a USB Ethernet adapter. Updating the driver has also solved similar problems previously.

This error is known; often, restarting the software or the PC resolves it and restores connection. Do you have multiple LAN interfaces? If yes, verify that the correct interface is selected before attempting connection. If the issue continues, let us know.

Reporting back: Installation of [product_name] software [version_no] on a laptop with Windows 7 Ultimate 64bit works fine and I can send programs without issues. The network interface name is displayed correctly. On a desktop PC running Windows XP Pro SP3, there are two interfaces—a Realtek Ethernet and a TeamViewer VPN. Planning to update the Realtek driver and will report results.

I encountered the same communication problem. Changing my network card speed setting from 'auto' to 10 Mbps allowed downloads, though refresh stopped working. I've asked on another thread whether this behavior is typical.
You fixed my issue—thank you very much!

I solved the connection problem with [product_name] by checking drivers in VMware, disabling unused ones and leaving only the Ethernet connection active. Attached images show the changes. I hope this solution helps others facing similar challenges.
Please post in English if you intend to help, but thanks for sharing your solution—it is appreciated. Translation provided below.
Thanks for sharing feedback. I had originally posted in English, but it appears [well-known_company] auto-translated my message for some reason.

analysis.insight_summary: Multiple users experience ongoing connection issues between PC and [product_name] modules using [product_name] software [version_no], especially in virtual machines or when Ethernet interface configurations are complex or not recognized properly. Software detects network devices but fails to complete program transfers, with solutions that worked in previous versions no longer being effective. Problems seem related to how the latest software version manages network interfaces and device detection compared to earlier versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward and reliable connectivity and program transfer between [product_name] software [version_no] and hardware modules, regardless of machine type, operating system, or network card setup.
